findings.title: No per-key guard against concurrent BuildIndex now that the global lock is removed
findings.body:
`BuildIndex` used to run entirely under `cacheMu`. Now the lock is taken only to store the result. `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` does a check-then-build (`GetIndex` returns nil, then `build`), so two callers can build the same `NamespacedResource` concurrently. Typical callers are two `Search` requests, or a `Search` request racing the async `handleEvent` watcher. The consequences are:
- Duplicate full ListIterator scans.
- The second cache store silently replaces the first index, so writes made to the losing instance are lost.
- `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics are double-counted.
- For file-based indexes, `bleve.New` on the same directory fails because the path already exists.

The code needs per-key build deduplication, e.g. singleflight or a per-key mutex, rather than either one global lock or none.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock. Builds can now run concurrently and write to the map under `cacheMu.Lock`, from `handleEvent` or `Search` triggering `getOrCreateIndex`. A concurrent map read/write is a data race and can crash with a fatal "concurrent map iteration and map write". Take `cacheMu.RLock()` while iterating.

findings.title: Shared variables mutated from errgroup goroutines in init
findings.body: Each goroutine in `init` assigns the outer `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization. Both are data races. The PR's goal is to raise indexing concurrency, which makes this more likely to trigger. Use a local `err` inside each goroutine and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Stop no longer causes requests to be rejected
findings.body: All per-request `s.Init(ctx)` checks were removed, but `Stop` still sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped". That error used to be returned to callers via `Init` after stop. Now nothing reads it, so requests after `Stop` reach the backend after the watch context is cancelled and the backend's `Stop` has run, instead of failing cleanly. The `initErr` writes in `Stop` are dead code, and the shutdown contract has silently changed.

findings.title: Context and lifecycle resources leaked when Init fails in the constructor
findings.body: If `s.Init(ctx)` fails, `NewResourceServer` returns nil without calling `cancel()`. It also does not stop a lifecycle that may already have been initialized, such as the DB backend. The background context and any goroutines started during partial init, like the search watch poller, are leaked. Call `cancel()` (and `lifecycle.Stop` where appropriate) on the error path.

findings.title: Integration test disabled for postgres without a tracked fix
findings.body: The storage-server module test is now skipped on postgres, with the note "Works locally". This lands alongside a change that moves DB initialization and index building into server construction, which is exactly what this test exercises. Skipping it removes coverage that could catch startup regressions caused by this PR.
